request: Use geometry of cylindrical hole defined in Sketch4 for creating inscribed hexagonal polygonal to the original hole and make it through all cutout instead.

actions.operation: Create a hexagonal polygon profile using the cylindrical-hole geometry defined in Sketch4.

parameters.constraint_type: inscribed in the original Sketch4 circle
parameters.profile_center: Concentric with the existing box-end eye bore, approximately x=0 and z=10 mm
parameters.sketch_plane: Upper planar eye land at y=15 mm, normal to the wrench thickness direction
parameters.orientation: Retain as unresolved unless Sketch4 contains an existing angular or horizontal/vertical constraint

actions.target: The original cylindrical-hole profile defined in Sketch4.
actions.relational_constraint: The hexagonal polygon must be inscribed in the original cylindrical-hole profile.
actions.unresolved_reference: Identify the circular Sketch4 entity defining the original cylindrical hole. The rotational orientation of the inscribed hexagon is not specified.
steps: Localize the requested geometry at the positive-z box end, Section S03. The existing cylindrical hole is the Eye bore labeled face_code 0016, corresponding to STEP Brep_id FACE 21 and having a nominal radius of 10 mm.

Use the continuous upper body land labeled face_code 0010, STEP Brep_id FACE 24, specifically its annular box-end region, as the planar sketch support if Sketch4 must be recreated. This face lies at y=15 mm and is perpendicular to the through-thickness cut direction.

Open and edit Sketch4 rather than sketching on the open-ended jaw or the handle recess. Confirm that the referenced circle is concentric with the outer eye circumference and centered approximately at x=0, z=10 mm.

Retain the original circular entity as construction geometry, or project its circular edge into the sketch as associative construction geometry, so that it controls the replacement polygon without remaining as a closed cutting contour.
Create a regular six-sided polygon using a center-and-vertex polygon tool. Constrain its center coincident with the center of the original Sketch4 circle.

Apply an inscribed relationship by constraining all six polygon vertices to the original radius-10-mm construction circle. For a regular hexagon, this gives a 20 mm across-corners size and an approximately 17.3205 mm across-flats size.
Apply equal-length constraints to all six sides and the necessary regular-polygon angular constraints. Fully constrain translation using the concentric center relation.

Do not infer a polygon rotation from the cylindrical bore because a circle has no angular datum. If no existing Sketch4 orientation constraint is available, leave the hexagon rotation unresolved for design confirmation; otherwise preserve the pre-existing horizontal, vertical, or angular reference.
Remove the original circle from the active cutting profile or convert it to construction geometry. The final active sketch region must contain only one closed regular hexagonal loop.
Verify that the hexagonal loop lies completely inside the annular outer eye boundary represented by face_code 0015 and does not intersect either eye-to-handle transition.

actions.operation: Create or modify the cutout using the inscribed hexagonal polygon with a through-all extent, replacing the original hole cutout.

parameters.cut_direction: Normal to Sketch4 through the full y=15 mm to y=0 mm body thickness
parameters.feature_replacement: Suppress or redefine the original cylindrical-hole cut before applying the hexagonal cut
parameters.edge_treatment: No chamfer or fillet unless separately specified

actions.target: The inscribed hexagonal polygon created in the previous action and the original hole cutout it replaces.
actions.relational_constraint: The cutout must pass completely through the affected solid rather than retain the original cylindrical-hole cutout.
actions.unresolved_reference: Identify the solid body to cut, the cut direction, and the existing cylindrical-hole feature that must be replaced or suppressed.
steps: Locate the existing cylindrical bore feature that produces face_code 0016, STEP Brep_id FACE 21. This cylindrical face is the geometry to be removed and replaced by six planar internal faces.

Suppress the original cylindrical-hole cut or edit its parent feature so that the circular profile no longer removes material. This sequencing is mandatory because an inscribed hexagon is smaller than its circumcircle; adding a hexagonal cut to the already cylindrical opening cannot restore the material between the hexagon flats and the original circular boundary.

If the model is history-based, redefine the existing bore feature to consume the edited Sketch4 hexagonal profile. If the model is an imported history-free solid, first reconstruct or heal the circular bore with an annular plug united to the box-end rim, then perform the hexagonal subtraction.
Select the single closed hexagonal region in Sketch4 and create a subtractive extrusion or pocket feature.

Set the termination to Through All so the cut traverses the complete nominal 15 mm wrench thickness, from the upper side at y=15 mm through the lower side at y=0 mm. Reverse the extrusion direction if the preview points away from the solid.

Limit the operation to the single wrench solid. The cut must affect Section S03, the box-end eye, without cutting the central handle, upper handle recess, open-ended jaw, or the outer eye circumference.

Regenerate the model. The original cylindrical Eye bore face_code 0016 will cease to exist and will be replaced by six new planar internal faces; these new faces do not yet have face_code values in the supplied model.json.

Confirm that the upper opening boundary modifies the box-end portion of face_code 0010, STEP Brep_id FACE 24, and that the through-all exit modifies the box-end portion of face_code 0014, STEP Brep_id FACE 25.

Inspect the top and bottom views to verify that the opening is hexagonal on both sides and coaxial through the thickness. Inspect the front, back, left, right, and isometric views to verify complete penetration and the absence of residual cylindrical wall segments.
Check that the annular torque-transfer rim remains continuous around the new opening and that all six socket faces are planar, equal in width, and parallel to the cut direction.
Do not add chamfers, countersinks, or internal fillets because none are requested. Preserve sharp hexagonal entry and exit edges unless manufacturing requirements are supplied separately.
Recompute mass and section properties if required, and validate that the resulting model remains one watertight solid with a single through-all hexagonal opening at the box end.

intention: Replace the original cylindrical-hole cutout with an inscribed hexagonal through-all cutout; no additional functional purpose is explicitly stated.
Modify the closed fastener interface of Section S03 while preserving the outer eye rim, handle transitions, handle recess, and open-ended jaw.
Use the existing Sketch4 circle as associative construction geometry so the replacement hexagon remains concentric and dimensionally controlled by the original 10 mm bore radius.
